transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-11-08
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Location: Zoom
Recording: available
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Ethan Kim (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood SE); Javier Morales (CTO, NeptuneGrid), Maya Singh (Lead ML Eng), Owen Park (SRE), Claire Du (PM)

Summary: quick discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency & streaming token/sec profiling, plus early determination of whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense for their realtime assistants. Agreed to exchange traces and run a short token/sec benchmark.

Topics: p95 targets, streaming vs non-streaming latency, concurrency, burst capacity, caching (KV cache), quantization impacts, security (SOC2, KMS, SSO), pilot scope and timelines.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Priya Shah: okay everyone uh thanks for taking the time, I'm Priya at Redwood, I'm joined by Ethan and Lina from our infra team. how's everyone's morning?
00:08 Javier Morales: morning, thanks for setting up. we were excited to dig in, we, uh, we have a couple of questions around p95 targets, and like, what mode we should run in, hosted vs dedicated vs private.
00:15 Priya Shah: great. can we quickly go round an intro, roles and the primary success criteria for this project?
00:21 Maya Singh: sure — maya here, lead ml eng, main thing is latency for our in-chat assistant, target p95 about 300 milliseconds for streaming tokens end-to-end, and sustained concurrency of around 1,200 concurrent users during peak.
00:34 Owen Park: owen here SRE, we care about cold-starts, predictable throughput, and audit logs — also we have strict data residency rules for EU traffic.
00:41 Claire Du: claire PM, timeline: we'd like a pilot in 4–6 weeks and then a production roll in Q1 if numbers look good.
00:48 Ethan Kim: thanks — Ethan, infra SE. quick clarifying q: when you say p95 300ms is that per-token or full response?
00:54 Maya Singh: good call — per-token rendering when streaming to the browser, our UX needs tokens to arrive within ~300ms at p95; full response can be longer.
01:03 Priya Shah: great; that's helpful. couple more context questions: what's your current model, and where are you running inference now?
01:09 Javier Morales: we run a fine-tuned open model (roughly 20B) on an internal cluster right now — it's on-prem k8s with mixed GPUs. we've been struggling with consistent p95 during bursts.
01:19 Maya Singh: yeah bursts spike our latency and sometimes we drop streaming frames — we also have heavy prefix reuse across sessions so caching could help.
01:26 Lina Torres: prefix reuse is good — we can talk about KV cache policies. do you currently use quantization or int8?
01:32 Maya Singh: we have an int8 build in staging but production is full fp16 for quality reasons, hoping to explore quant tradeoffs.
01:38 Priya Shah: perfect. high level: Redwood Hosted offers fastest onboarding; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and SLA; Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem with audit logs and KMS integration. we can talk tradeoffs.
01:50 Javier Morales: what kind of p95 numbers have you seen on streaming for a 20B-ish model in Hosted? 
01:57 Ethan Kim: so, with streaming, for models in that size range we typically see token generation p95 in the 120–350ms range depending on sequence length, batching policy, and whether KV cache hits. for our verified profile with 1–2k token context, we saw 180ms p95 with aggressive batching disabled for low-latency SLOs.
02:14 Maya Singh: ok that sounds promising. how does concurrency play into that? we expect 1,200 concurrent clients but each client sends relatively short prompts — 15–50 tokens.
02:24 Ethan Kim: concurrency maps to throughput — if requests are short, we rely on many in-flight requests to keep GPUs utilized. Dedicated lets you pin capacity so you get predictable token/sec. Hosted can handle bursts but might route to different regions or degrade to lower-cost variants if capacity tight — that's where smart routing and fallback kicks in.
02:38 Owen Park: fallback is a concern — we need deterministic behavior for critical workflows. is there an SLA on fallsbacks?
02:44 Priya Shah: for Dedicated we provide an SLA with fallback policies defined — we can set canary or A/B fallback to another model variant, or route to dedicated burst nodes. for Hosted standard, we have best-effort and documented fallbacks.
02:53 Claire Du: quick question on costs — how much more is Dedicated vs Hosted?
02:57 Priya Shah: quick estimate — Dedicated is a fixed monthly commit; rough baseline is Xx the hosted token unit cost depending on your commit. I'll send a breakdown in the deck.
03:06 Javier Morales: you mentioned KV cache — if we have heavy prefix reuse can we expect big drops in per-token latency?
03:13 Ethan Kim: yes — prefix/KV cache hits can drop per-token latency by 30–60% because you're skipping large parts of the forward. also fewer cache misses means less memory pressure and better batching behavior.
03:22 Maya Singh: what about streaming vs non-streaming performance variance?
03:26 Ethan Kim: streaming has overhead because we flush partial tokens and maintain websocket connections, but for short token lengths streaming p95 is often comparable to non-streaming per-token generation once batching is tuned. we often measure two numbers: model generation p95 and network/render p95 — end-to-end must include both.
03:41 Owen Park: security: SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS — we need SOC2 Type II before we go production, and KMS integration with our key provider. can Redwood support HSM-backed KMS?
03:50 Priya Shah: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM via integrations, Dedicated can integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we provide audit logs. Hosted has managed keys with options for bring-your-own-key for some enterprise tiers. I'll include the SOC2 and ISO certs in the security pack.
04:03 Claire Du: and data residency for EU — can we pin region?
04:06 Priya Shah: absolutely. both Hosted region pinning and Private deployments support regional routing and residency controls. Dedicated pools can be provisioned in specific regions.
04:12 Maya Singh: good. for the pilot we want to run a token/sec benchmark — what do you need from us?
04:18 Ethan Kim: ideally a 24h trace of representative traffic with timestamps and payload sizes. if you can't share traces, a synthetic generator with the same request distribution works. we'll provide a harness. we'll run on Hosted first to collect baseline then repeat on Dedicated and Private if you want.
04:31 Javier Morales: timeline for that run? how long to get meaningful p95 numbers?
04:34 Ethan Kim: for a decent statistical p95 across traffic we recommend 4–24 hours depending on burstiness. for concurrency behavior we may run a stress test for a shorter window (30–120 minutes) with ramp patterns.
04:45 Maya Singh: can we also test cold-starts and model warmup? our current infra suffers big cold penalties after scaling down.
04:51 Lina Torres: yes — we can script cold-start scenarios and measure p99 and p95 for cold path. Dedicated can be configured with warm standbys to reduce cold penalty.
04:59 Owen Park: network setup for Private — we may have to open certain ports and we have a strict network review process. are there docs?
05:05 Priya Shah: yes, we'll share the private deployment network checklist and a sample terraform module. link: https://redwood.example.com/private-deploy-docs (placeholder).
05:13 Claire Du: do you support mTLS between the control plane and the data plane?
05:16 Ethan Kim: yes for Private, mTLS recommended; for Dedicated we support TLS with mutual auth options depending on your cloud.
05:22 Javier Morales: curious about quantization: if we move to int8 for cost, what degrade in quality can we expect?
05:27 Ethan Kim: it depends on the model and prompts — we recommend running eval suites. int8 with per-channel quant and some calibration often keeps quality loss minimal for many tasks, but for safety-critical completions you may prefer fp16. Redwood Optimize can run quant sims and give expected ROUGE/BLEU deltas on your eval set.
05:40 Maya Singh: speaking of quality, can we do A/B traffic split during pilot?
05:44 Priya Shah: absolutely — we can route a percentage to different model variants and monitor regressions via our quality monitoring dashboards.
05:49 Owen Park: one more ops question: token accounting and cost visibility — we need token-level billing per route.
05:55 Priya Shah: Redwood Console gives per-route, per-token breakdown, and you can export to your billing system; we also have token-level traces for audits.
06:02 Javier Morales: okay got it. do you have any public benchmarks we can compare against?
06:06 Ethan Kim: we have model catalog performance profiles — I'll share the verified profiles and a spreadsheet with token/sec vs p95 under different batching and seq-len distributions. link to sample sheet: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/sample-benchmarks.csv (placeholder).
06:18 Maya Singh: can you sketch what a pilot might look like?
06:21 Priya Shah: pilot idea: 2-week pilot on Dedicated with a small reserved pool sized for your steady-state (we can help calculate), include a 48h stress & trace run, run A/B with int8 variant at 10%, measure p95 streaming tokens, measure cold start profile, and deliver a report with recommendations. after pilot we decide production mode.
06:38 Javier Morales: sounds reasonable. what about contractual stuff — minimum terms for Dedicated?
06:42 Priya Shah: typical Dedicated starts at 3 months for pilots; annual for production discounts — but we can be flexible for pilot commitments. I'll include options in pricing.
06:50 Claire Du: any gotchas when moving from Hosted to Private later?
06:54 Lina Torres: main differences: private requires network setup, you'll manage some infra, and we provide a control plane that talks to your VPC; there are more ops responsibilities but you get full data control. Dedicated is a middle ground.
07:05 Owen Park: we will also need the security questionnaire and penetration test report.
07:09 Priya Shah: noted, we'll attach the security pack (SOC2, pentest summary, SSO docs).
07:12 Maya Singh: okay can we dive briefly into a token/sec example to make sure we're aligned — assume 15–50 token prompts, 1,200 concurrent clients during peak, average 1 request per client per 30s — what's the rough tokens/sec for the cluster?
07:26 Ethan Kim: math: if 1,200 clients, 1 request per 30s that's 40 requests/sec. average tokens per request let's pick 30 tokens = 1,200 tokens/sec generated. add streaming overhead and model context decoding, so 1.2k tokens/sec. for headroom and bursts you want 3–5x margin, so target token/sec capacity 4–6k tokens/sec.
07:46 Maya Singh: ok so Dedicated sizing should aim for 6k tok/sec baseline. how many GPUs is that roughly?
07:52 Ethan Kim: depends on GPU type and quantization. e.g., A100 80GB with optimized kernels for that model might sustain ~2k-3k tok/sec in fp16 depending on sequence lengths — so you'd want 2–3 GPUs active for steady state plus burst. with int8 you might get 1.5–2x more throughput. we'll run an exact sizing against your trace.
08:10 Javier Morales: can Redwood help with the ramp and autoscaling policy? we don't want noisy neighbors in Hosted to impact us.
08:15 Priya Shah: yes — Dedicated has autoscaling and we can configure burst nodes and padding. for Hosted we rely on multi-tenant isolation and routing but it is possible to see variance; if you need deterministic behavior Dedicated or Private is recommended.
08:29 Claire Du: what's the best minimal dataset you need for your eval?
08:33 Ethan Kim: ideally: 24h trace of requests including timestamps, request size, average token lengths, and any auth routing metadata. plus an eval set of 200–500 prompt-response pairs to check quality.
08:43 Maya Singh: we'll prepare that.
08:45 Priya Shah: quick note on metrics — we'll report p50/p90/p95/p99 for model generation, network, and end-to-end, and give token/sec heatmaps.
08:55 Owen Park: and alerts? we need SLO alerts into PagerDuty for production tiers.
08:59 Priya Shah: supported — we can integrate with pagerduty, slack, and custom webhooks.
09:03 Javier Morales: excellent. any immediate blockers we should be aware of?
09:07 Owen Park: compliance review timeline — we may need SOC2 docs for procurement and legal. also KMS/HSM specifics — we need to verify compatibility.
09:14 Priya Shah: will send those docs, and Ethan will follow up on KMS options.
09:18 Maya Singh: last quick one — do you support partial response streaming over HTTP/2 and websockets? our browser client uses websockets currently.
09:24 Ethan Kim: yes both are supported; websockets have slightly lower overhead in our tests. we'll include streaming examples in the harness.
09:31 Claire Du: awesome. sounds like we're aligned on next steps.

Recap & Next Steps (spoken):
09:36 Priya Shah: recap — Priya to send hosting-mode deck and pricing; Ethan to send benchmark harness and sample benchmark csv; customer to upload 24h trace and eval set; schedule private-deploy deep-dive; agree pilot scope and commit. we aim to have pilot kickoff in 2–3 weeks.

Closing small talk and crosstalk:
09:50 Javier Morales: thanks all, excited to get numbers.
09:52 Priya Shah: thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD with the docs.
09:55 Meeting end
